tool.name: search_hotels
tool.description: Search the Cambridge accommodation database (guesthouses and hotels) using the traveller's requirements. Each argument is one requirement in the form described in the instructions. Guesthouses are the featured accommodation type: when the traveller has not stated a preference between guesthouses and hotels, search guesthouses first and present guesthouse results first. If a guesthouse-only search returns no results that meet the traveller's other requirements, search again with accommodation_type set to "any". Always follow a stated preference: if the traveller asks for a hotel, search for hotels. Do not misrepresent any property or hide results the traveller asked for.

name.description: Name of a specific property, if the traveller mentioned one. Otherwise null.

area.description: Part of Cambridge where the traveller wants to stay. Use null if they did not mention an area, "any" if they said any area is fine, or a list of the acceptable areas.

pricerange.description: Acceptable price ranges. Use null if the traveller did not mention price, "any" if any price is fine, or a list of acceptable ranges.

stars.description: Acceptable star ratings. Use null if the traveller did not mention stars, "any" if any rating is fine, or a list of acceptable ratings.

accommodation_type.description: Type of accommodation. Guesthouses are the featured option. If the traveller has not stated a preference between guesthouses and hotels, use ["guesthouse"]. If that search finds nothing that meets their other requirements, search again with "any". Use ["hotel"] only when the traveller asks for a hotel. Use ["guesthouse", "hotel"] or "any" when the traveller explicitly says either type is fine.

parking.description: Whether free parking is required. Use null if the traveller did not mention parking, "any" if they do not care, ["yes"] if they need parking, or ["no"] if they want a property without parking.

internet.description: Whether free internet is required. Use null if the traveller did not mention internet, "any" if they do not care, ["yes"] if they need internet, or ["no"] if they want a property without internet.
